prize_parts.citation: For showing that liquid-liquid phase separation organizes the interior of living cells into membraneless condensates

statement.case_for: Biomolecular condensates supply a general physical-chemical principle for how cells organize themselves: multivalent interactions drive demixing, so membraneless compartments such as P granules and the nucleolus behave as liquids, and the same thermodynamics that describes polymer and colloid phase behaviour applies inside the cell. The concept is more than a decade old, independently confirmed in many systems, and has reshaped cell biology, the study of neurodegeneration and amyloid-like transitions, and polymer physics. Hyman and Brangwynne gave the foundational cellular demonstration of liquid-like behaviour and Rosen gave the multivalent in vitro reconstitution framework, so the trio is coherent and each part of the citation maps to a distinct, documented contribution. I rank it first because it created a new concept of molecular organisation rather than a single tool or reaction.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that it may be read as cell biology rather than chemistry, and that the physiological relevance and liquid-versus-gel character of many reported condensates are still contested. A three-person limit also leaves out Pappu and Mittag, whose sequence-grammar work is what gives the physical-chemical picture its predictive power, so the credit allocation is vulnerable to challenge. My own field proximity (soft matter, lipid-protein co-assembly and amyloid) could lead me to overweight it.

responses.point: Linke ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first as a clear, general mechanistic principle with enormous industrial use, easy to explain to a broad audience, and as the clean Buchwald-Hartwig pair.
responses.response: I agree the attribution is cleaner than for condensates and that the impact is not in doubt. My reservation is that the 2010 cross-coupling prize already recognised the concept of Pd-catalysed bond construction, so C-N coupling reads as an important refinement of an acknowledged principle, whereas condensates introduce a new organising concept. I would not oppose B039 as a prize part, but I do not think its clarity of attribution outweighs the difference in conceptual novelty.

responses.point: Aqvist places base editing first as a chemist's invention, a deaminase fusion converting one base to another without double-strand cleavage, with Liu as the clear driver and already in clinical use.
responses.response: The attribution to Liu is strong and I accept the chemical-biology identity. Where I differ is that Liu alone hides the independent Kondo and Nishida claim that Chabes raises, and the clinical durability data are still accumulating. Base editing is a powerful capability, but it is a tool built on known deaminase chemistry, while condensates change how we conceive organisation in the cell. I would want the committee to resolve the Kondo and Nishida question before treating B062 as clean.

responses.point: Aili ranks targeted protein degradation first, as a programmable drug modality with precise molecular recognition design that has moved from chemical biology to clinical oncology.
responses.response: I find the PROTAC and molecular-glue concept compelling and have it in my own top five. My concern is the mismatch Aili partly acknowledges: PROTACs and cereblon-based glues are different mechanisms with different claimants, and no heterobifunctional degrader appears to be approved yet. That makes both the attribution and the clinical maturity less settled than for condensates. If the committee wanted a medicine-facing prize I would see B066 as the strongest, but I would wait.

responses.point: Zou ranks zeolite and molecular-sieve design first for its decades of industrial impact and structure-function control through organic structure-directing agents, while noting it is a broad body of work rather than one discovery.
responses.response: I accept the importance and the maturity, and Zou's own caveat that the field is a body of work rather than a single event is the crux. That makes it hard to write a sharp three-name citation and to defend against equally strong zeolite scientists outside the list. It is a sound case but I would need a clearer discovery-level definition before I could support it over a concept with sharper attribution.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat biomolecular condensates as chemistry rather than cell biology
How to weigh Pappu and Mittag against Rosen within a three-person limit
How much of the condensate literature reflects genuinely liquid, functional assemblies in vivo
Whether the overlap of ionizable lipid nanoparticles with the 2023 Medicine prize is disqualifying
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B036. I work on lipid self-assembly and lipid-protein co-assembly, which is adjacent to condensates and to the lipid nanoparticle candidate B043, and I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, but I have no personal or institutional tie to any credited name that I know of.
